HPV-associated vaginitis and cervicitis

In one randomized trial, adding red light to high-dose interferon produced higher 12-week HPV clearance and vaginitis or cervicitis cure rates than interferon alone. This supports the combination studied, not PBM used by itself.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In one randomized trial, adding red light to high-dose interferon produced higher 12-week HPV clearance and vaginitis or cervicitis cure rates than interferon alone. This supports the combination studied, not PBM used by itself.

Summary of the Evidence

One three-arm randomized study of 90 women examined red-light treatment added to interferon for subclinical or latent HPV infection associated with vaginitis or cervicitis. The study compared low-dose interferon, high-dose interferon, and high-dose interferon plus red light. No duplicate report, independent replication, animal experiment, or laboratory study was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

At 12 weeks, HPV clearance was reported in 86.5% of the combination group, compared with 68.8% of the high-dose interferon group and 27.1% of the low-dose group. Vaginitis or cervicitis cure was reported in 87.5% with combination treatment and 50.0% with high-dose interferon alone. Three of 30 participants in the combination group had mild adverse effects. These findings favor adding light to the high-dose interferon regimen tested, but the design cannot isolate the contribution of PBM as well as a factorial or sham-light comparison could (Shi et al. 2018).

Animal evidence

No animal study directly addressing HPV-associated vaginitis or cervicitis was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The publication used 625-nm red visible light delivered to the cervical and vaginal region over a four-week treatment course. The database reports approximately 20 minutes per exposure, but the irradiance values are inconsistent and the number of individual sessions is not clearly documented. The study tested light as an adjunct to high-dose interferon, not as monotherapy. The results therefore apply to that combination and its short follow-up, not to PBM alone or long-term viral clearance.

Interpretation

The combination group had higher short-term HPV clearance and clinical cure rates than the high-dose interferon-only group. This is a positive randomized result for adjunctive treatment in one study. Independent replication is needed to determine whether light adds benefit and whether the difference persists beyond 12 weeks.

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Low for improved short-term HPV clearance with red light added to interferon.

Rationale for the certainty assessment

One randomized 90-person study found higher 12-week clearance and cure rates when red light was added to high-dose interferon. Because the intervention combined light and medication and has not been independently repeated, the light contribution and durability are unresolved. A replicated trial with sham light, longer virologic follow-up, and cervical outcomes would support a stronger rating.
